# Adjudication Task — Chapter 224

## Korean source

```text
  1|＃224화
  2|
  3|
  4|
  5|몇 시간 전, 전력을 다해 게이트 입구로 돌아가던 십여 명의 스타 길드원들을 멈춰 세운 것은 원명훈의 외침이었다.
  6|
  7|“잠깐, 모두 정지!”
  8|
  9|모두의 시선이 그를 향해 쏠렸다.
 10|
 11|당장 뒤에서 무시무시한 네임드 몬스터가 등장할지도 모른다는 긴장감 속, 홀로 골똘히 생각에 잠겨 있던 원명훈의 입술이 열렸다.
 12|
 13|“정찰.”
 14|
 15|“예. 길드장님.”
 16|
 17|정찰 임무를 맡은 길드원이 즉각 대답했다.
 18|
 19|발이 빠르고 활을 잘 다루는 그는 제비뽑기라는 행운 덕분에 다른 동료들과 달리 간신히 죽음을 피했다.
 20|
 21|“현 위치 읊어 봐.”
 22|
 23|“좌표상 175. 37. 990입니다.”
 24|
 25|“좌표는 지랄, 게이트 입구까지 얼마 남았냐고.”
 26|
 27|“지금까지 속도를 봤을 때 약 7분 정도가 소요될 것 같습니다.”
 28|
 29|“얼마 안 남았네? 게이트 입구로 가는 길은 이곳뿐이지?”
 30|
 31|“……예. 그렇긴 합니다만.”
 32|
 33|정찰대원이 찝찝한 얼굴로 말꼬리를 흐렸다.
 34|
 35|뭔가 이상한 흐름을 느낀 다른 길드원들도 눈빛을 주고받던 그때, 불안감을 현실로 만드는 한 마디가 들려왔다.
 36|
 37|“여기서 포위망 펼친다.”
 38|
 39|“예?”
 40|
 41|“포위망이라니. 이 상황에서 말입니까?”
 42|
 43|“길드장님, 그건!”
 44|
 45|평소였다면 군말 없이 따랐을 길드원들의 반발에 원명훈의 눈빛이 차갑게 식었다.
 46|
 47|“다들 닥치고 명령 따라. 내가 다 생각이 있어서 그런 거니까.”
 48|
 49|“그래도 이건 아닙니다! 상대는 네임드 몬스터, 컥!”
 50|
 51|가장 크게 목소리를 높이던 길드원의 목을 잡아챈 원명훈이 으르렁거렸다.
 52|
 53|“게이트에서, 그것도 길드장 명령에 항명해? 이 새끼가 죽고 싶어서 환장했나…….”
 54|
 55|그야말로 순식간에 벌어진 일.
 56|
 57|장내의 분위기가 싸늘하게 얼어붙었다. 이 자리의 모두는 원명훈의 말이 비단 한 사람을 겨냥한 것이 아니라는 사실을 알고 있었다.
 58|
 59|지난 수년 동안 지켜본 바로는 능히 행동으로 옮길만한 위인이라는 것도.
 60|
 61|“죄, 죄송합니다.”
 62|
 63|“마지막 기회다. 두 번은 없어.”
 64|
 65|털썩.
 66|
 67|하얗게 질린 얼굴로 주저앉은 길드원을 뒤로하고 돌아선 원명훈이 날카로운 시선으로 주위를 훑었다.
 68|
 69|“병신 같은 놈들.”
 70|
 71|필터링을 거치지 않은 폭언에도 십여 쌍의 고개는 땅만 응시했다.
 72|
 73|이미 지난 수년 동안 원명훈이라는 인간을 충분히 겪어 본 그들에게는 익숙한 일이다.
 74|
 75|게이트에서는 더더욱 조심해야 했다. 그는 A급 헌터, 이 자리의 모두가 달려들어도 이길 수 없는 강자다.
 76|
 77|“대가리가 그렇게 안 굴러가나? 내가 네임드 몬스터를 상대할 만큼 멍청한 놈으로 보여?”
 78|
 79|푹 수그리고 있던 고개들이 슬그머니 올라왔다.
 80|
 81|“그럼…….”
 82|
 83|“그 떨거지들을 처리한다.”
 84|
 85|“떨거지들이라면, 평화 길드 말입니까?”
 86|
 87|“지금쯤이면 전멸하고도 남았을 것 같은데요.”
 88|
 89|그들은 정신없이 도망치는 와중에 괴수의 포효를 들었다. 듣는 것만으로도 오금이 저리고 등골이 오싹해지는, 그건 말 그대로 공포 그 자체였다.
 90|
 91|비록 어떻게 생긴 놈인지 확인은 못 했지만 그렇기에 지금까지 살아 있을 수 있었다.
 92|
 93|‘그런 놈을 겨우 다섯이서 어떻게 상대해. 이미 다 죽었지.’
 94|
 95|이것이 모두의 공통된 의견이었다.
 96|
 97|그러나 오직 한 사람, 원명훈만큼은 달랐다.
 98|
 99|“만약 한 놈이라도 살아남아 도망친다면?”
100|
101|“그, 그건…….”
102|
103|“설마요.”
104|
105|거기까지는 미처 생각해 보지 못한 문제다.
106|
107|평소였다면 달랐을 텐데, 네임드 몬스터에 대한 두려움과 생존 욕구가 불러온 사고의 마비였다.
108|
109|우물쭈물하는 길드원들을 향해 원명훈이 확고한 어조로 말했다.
110|
111|“만에 하나 그 떨거지 중에 단 한 놈이라도 살아서 게이트를 빠져나가면, 우리 전부 인생 종 치는 거다.”
112|
113|“…….”
114|
115|“언론의 스포트라이트를 듬뿍 받고 있던 A급 헌터가 죽었다. 그리고 유일하게 살아남은 평화 길드원 중 하나가 우리 이야기를 꺼낸다? 그 후는 굳이 말 안 해도 대충 알겠지.”
116|
117|언론, 아니 전 국민의 관심이 그들을 향해 쏠린다.
118|
119|수사기관이 움직이고, 언론과 대중 미디어는 이 문제를 매우 비중 있게 다루며 연일 새로운 보도를 쏟아 낼 것이다.
120|
121|설령 생존자가 명확한 증언과 물증을 제시하지 못한다고 해도, 그들이 받을 멸시와 비난은 사라지지 않는다.
122|
123|어쩌면 이 나라를 떠나야 할지도 모른다. 부모님 성묘를 위해 비자를 발급받아야 하는 처지. 상상만 해도 끔찍했다.
124|
125|“가끔은 사실보다는 사람들의 인식이 중요하지. 너희도 8년 전에 이미 겪어 봤잖아?”
126|
127|“길드장님!”
128|
129|“그건!”
130|
131|격렬한 동요가 스타 길드원들 사이로 퍼져 나갔다.
132|
133|그것은 암묵적인 금기어였다. 그런데 다름 아닌 원명훈이 직접 이런 이야기를 꺼낼 줄이야.
134|
135|심지어 그는 모든 일을 계획하고 자신들을 포섭했던 사람 아닌가?
136|
137|길드원들의 사나워진 눈빛에 원명훈이 피식 웃었다.
138|
139|“눈 깔아. 이 개새끼들아. 죄다 뽑아 버리기 전에.”
140|
141|“……!”
142|
143|“너희가 원해서 가담한 거잖아. 여기에 내 돈 안 받아먹은 새끼 있어? 그 돈으로 집 사고, 차 사고, 술이며 여자며 실컷 즐기다가 결혼해서 애 낳고. 좋은 아빠인 척, 성실한 남편인 척하면서 잘 살고 있잖아?”
144|
145|원명훈이 신경질적으로 머리카락을 쓸었다. 그의 번뜩이는 눈빛이 스쳐 지나갈 때마다 사람들의 몸이 떨렸다.
146|
147|부정하고 싶지만, 그의 입에서 나온 말은 모두 사실이었다.
148|
149|그들은 이미 돌아올 수 없는 강을 건넜고, 그들을 배에 실어 강 너머로 옮긴 건 원명훈이었다.
150|
151|뱃사공은 이미 배를 숨겼다. 그의 허락이 없다면 다시 강 저편으로 돌아갈 수 없다.
152|
153|숨이 끊기기 전까지는.
154|
155|“더 이상 길게 말 안 한다. 숨어서 포위망 펼쳐. 내 신호가 떨어지면 누구든 죽여 버릴 수 있게.”
156|
157|원명훈의 살기 어린 목소리는 대법원의 판결문이나 다름없었다.
158|
159|항소 따위는 통하지 않는다는 것을 깨달은 사람들이 뿔뿔이 흩어져 포위망을 형성하기 시작했다.
160|
161|“병신 같은 새끼들. 벌써 8년이나 지난 일을.”
162|
163|씹어뱉듯이 중얼거리던 원명훈에게 한 길드원이 쭈뼛거리며 다가왔다.
164|
165|“저, 길드장님.”
166|
167|“왜.”
168|
169|“1팀장님, 아니 1팀장은 어떻게 할까요?”
170|
171|“김종훈이? 그 새끼 지금 어디 있어?”
172|
173|“우선은 저기에 옮겨 놨습니다.”
174|
175|길드원이 가리키는 방향을 따라 고개를 돌린 원명훈이 헛웃음을 흘렸다.
176|
177|불과 몇 미터 앞, 창백하게 질린 채 이빨을 부딪치는 그는 뭔가에 홀린 사람 같았다.
178|
179|“한심한 새끼. 저딴 걸 A급 헌터라고 데리고 있던 내가 등신이지.”
180|
181|작게 혀를 찬 원명훈이 손을 내저었다.
182|
183|“소리 안 나게 알아서 처리해.”
184|
185|떠나려는 그에게 길드원이 다급한 목소리로 외쳤다.
186|
187|“예에? 저, 전 못 합니다!”
188|
189|“그게 무슨 소리야?”
190|
191|“사, 살인은 안 하겠다는 말입니다.”
192|
193|“뭐? 이 또라이 새끼가 도대체 무슨 생각을……. 아니, 잠깐만.”
194|
195|기가 찬 표정으로 길드원을 쥐어박으려던 원명훈이 멈칫했다.
196|
197|본래 지시하려고 했던 것은 침묵 마법이든, 뭐든 조용히 있게 만들라는 지시였다. 하지만 그럴 필요가 있을까?
198|
199|‘생각해 보면 1팀장, 저놈만큼 내 비밀에 대해 잘 아는 놈도 없는데.’
200|
201|자그마치 10년을 수족으로 부렸던 녀석이다. 나름 잔대가리도 있었고, 헌터로서의 실력도 뛰어났다.
202|
203|8년 전 그 사건이 벌어졌을 때도 유일하게 한 사람, 1팀장만큼은 배신하지 않을 거라 믿었다.
204|
205|‘입을 열었다가는 저놈도 무사하지 못했을 테니까.’
206|
207|신뢰가 아니라 이해득실의 문제다. 비록 욕심의 크기는 다를지라도, 두 사람은 어떤 의미에서 동류라 할 수 있었다.
208|
209|하지만…….
210|
211|‘이제는 쓸모없어졌지.’
212|
213|원명훈은 지금껏 상위 몬스터의 피어(Fear)에 노출된 놈들을 여럿 봐 왔다. 제각각 증상의 차이는 있었지만 딱 하나 공통점이 있었다.
214|
215|‘폐품.’
216|
217|공포가 영혼에 각인된 자들은 두 번 다시 예전으로 돌아갈 수 없다.
218|
219|미쳐서 특수병동에 갇힌 사람도 있고, 간신히 회복하더라도 헌터로서의 인생은 끝장났다고 봐야 한다.
220|
221|‘내 비밀을 가장 많이 알고 있고, 예티의 목걸이를 직접 구해 온 것도 저놈이지.’
222|
223|거기에 더해 A급 헌터라는 명함도 종잇장이 되어 버렸다.
224|
225|원명훈이 고민한 시간은 짧았고, 결심은 더욱 빨랐다.
226|
227|“묶어 둬. 쓸 곳이 있으니까.”
228|
229|“예?”
230|
231|“네임드 몬스터. 그 괴물이 오면 던져 줄 먹잇감 하나쯤은 필요하지 않겠냐?”
232|
233|“……!”
234|
235|“여러모로 나쁘지 않아. 진태경이 죽었으니 우리 쪽도 A급 하나 정도는 끼워 줘야 그림이 살지.”
236|
237|얼어붙은 길드원의 어깨를 툭 치고 지나간 원명훈은 근처 수풀에 몸을 숨겼다.
238|
239|‘자, 누구든 와라.’
240|
241|기다림은 생각보다 길지 않았다.
242|
243|수십 미터 앞, 수풀을 헤치며 나타난 두 사람을 본 그의 입꼬리가 올라갔다.
244|
245|‘길드장 노인네에 진태경이라. 나머지는 다 죽었나?’
246|
247|전신에 피를 뒤집어쓴 진태경과 등에 업힌 늙은 마법사. 어떻게 보더라도 부상자에 패잔병의 몰골이다.
248|
249|‘일이 쉬워지겠군.’
250|
251|특히 진태경, 저 자식은 직접 죽이고 싶었다.
252|
253|원명훈이 길드원들에게 신호를 보낼 만반의 준비를 끝마친 그때였다.
254|
255|“나와, 이 시발 새끼들아.”
256|
257|정확히 자신이 숨은 수풀을 향해 손가락을 까딱이는 진태경의 모습에, 원명훈의 입가에 맺혀 있던 미소가 자취를 감췄다.
258|
259|
260|
261|* * *
262|
263|
264|
265|“이런 싸가지 없는 새끼를 봤나.”
266|
267|일그러진 원명훈의 얼굴을 보니 절로 실소가 새어 나왔다.
268|
269|뭐랄까, 한 인간의 밑바닥을 제대로 본 것 같아서.
270|
271|“웃어?”
272|
273|그런 내 모습이 화를 돋운 모양이다. 마른 입술을 핥은 그가 뜨거운 숨을 토해 냈다.
274|
275|“너 이 새끼…… 지금 상황 파악 안 되냐?”
276|
277|“아주 잘 되는데.”
278|
279|“그런 놈이 실실 쪼개?”
280|
281|“단어 선택 잘해라. 그런 말 들으면 네 대가리를 쪼개 버리고 싶어지잖아.”
282|
283|“……뭐?”
284|
285|“원명훈 씨, 라고 불러 줬을 때 멈췄어야지. 원명훈 씨발 새끼야.”
286|
287|하이에나들의 표정이 순간 멍해졌다.
288|
289|한참이나 꾹 닫혀 있던 원명훈의 입술이 가까스로 열렸다.
290|
291|“미쳤냐?”
292|
293|“나야 늘 멀쩡하지. 안 그래요, 김 집사님?”
294|

“I—I’m sorry.”

[P31]
“This is your last chance. There won’t be another.”

[P32]
Thud.

[P33]
The Guild member collapsed to the ground, his face white. Won Myunghoon turned away and swept a sharp gaze over the others.

[P34]
“Fucking idiots.”

[P35]
Even in the face of his unfiltered abuse, a dozen pairs of eyes remained fixed on the ground.

[P36]
They had spent years dealing with Won Myunghoon. This was nothing new.

[P37]
They had to be even more careful around him inside a Gate. He was an A-Rank Hunter—a powerhouse none of them could defeat even if they attacked him together.

[P38]
“Do your brains not work? Do I look stupid enough to take on a Named Monster?”

[P39]
The bowed heads slowly began to rise.

[P40]
“Then…”

[P41]
“We’ll deal with those losers.”

[P42]
“You mean the Peace Guild?”

[P43]
“By now, they should all be dead.”

[P44]
While fleeing in a panic, they had heard the monster’s roar. Just hearing it had weakened their knees and sent chills down their spines. It was terror itself.

[P45]
They hadn’t even seen what the creature looked like, and that was precisely why they were still alive.

[P46]
*How could five people possibly fight something like that? They must all be dead by now.*

[P47]
Every one of them shared that opinion.

[P48]
Everyone except Won Myunghoon.

[P49]
“What if even one of them survives and escapes?”

[P50]
“Th—that…”

[P51]
“No way.”

[P52]
They hadn’t considered that possibility.

[P53]
Under normal circumstances, they might have. But fear of the Named Monster and their desperate will to survive had paralyzed their minds.

[P54]
Won Myunghoon addressed the hesitant Guild members in a firm voice.

[P55]
“If even one of those losers gets out of the Gate alive, every last one of us is finished.”

[P56]
“…….”

[P57]
“An A-Rank Hunter who’s been soaking up the media spotlight dies, and then one of the surviving Peace Guild members starts talking about us? I don’t need to explain what happens next, do I?”

[P58]
The media’s attention—no, the entire country’s—would turn toward them.

[P59]
Investigators would get involved. The press and broadcast media would treat it as a major story, churning out new reports day after day.

[P60]
Even if the survivor couldn’t provide definitive testimony or physical evidence, the contempt and condemnation directed at them would never disappear.

[P61]
They might even have to flee the country, reduced to applying for visas just to visit their parents’ graves.

[P62]
The thought alone was horrifying.

[P63]
“Sometimes, what people believe matters more than the truth. You all learned that eight years ago, didn’t you?”

[P64]
“Guild Master!”

[P65]
“That’s—!”

[P66]
The Star Guild members erupted in agitation.

[P67]
It was an unspoken taboo, yet Won Myunghoon himself had brought it up.

[P68]
Wasn’t he the one who had planned everything and recruited them in the first place?

[P69]
As their gazes hardened, Won Myunghoon let out a quiet laugh.

[P70]
“Eyes down, you fucking bastards. Before I rip them all out.”

[P71]
“……!”

[P72]
“You joined because you wanted to. Is there a single bastard here who didn’t take my money? You used it to buy houses and cars, drink and chase women, then got married and had kids. Now you’re all living comfortably, pretending to be good fathers and devoted husbands. Aren’t you?”

[P73]
Won Myunghoon irritably ran a hand through his hair. Whenever his gleaming eyes swept over them, they trembled.

[P74]
They wanted to deny it, but every word out of his mouth was true.

[P75]
They had already crossed a river from which there was no return, and Won Myunghoon was the one who had ferried them to the other side.

[P76]
The ferryman had already hidden the boat. Without his permission, they could never return to the opposite bank.

[P77]
Not while they still drew breath.

[P78]
“I’m done talking. Hide and set up the cordon. When I give the signal, be ready to kill whoever comes.”

[P79]
Won Myunghoon’s voice, thick with killing intent, might as well have been a verdict handed down by the Supreme Court.

[P80]
Realizing there would be no appeal, the Guild members scattered and began forming the cordon.

[P81]
“Fucking idiots. It’s already been eight years…”

[P82]
As Won Myunghoon spat the words through clenched teeth, one of the Guild members cautiously approached him.

[P83]
“Guild Master.”

[P84]
“What?”

[P85]
“Team Leader 1, sir—I mean, what should we do with Team Leader 1?”

[P86]
“Kim Jonghun? Where the hell is that bastard?”

[P87]
“We moved him over there for now.”

[P88]
Won Myunghoon looked where the Guild member was pointing and let out a hollow laugh.

[P89]
Only a few meters away, Kim Jonghun sat deathly pale, his teeth chattering. He looked like a man possessed.

[P90]
“Pathetic bastard. I was the idiot for keeping something like that around and calling him an A-Rank Hunter.”

[P91]
Won Myunghoon clicked his tongue and waved a hand.

[P92]
“Take care of him quietly.”

[P93]
“What? I—I can’t!”

[P94]
“What the hell does that mean?”

[P95]
“I mean I won’t commit murder.”

[P96]
“What? What the hell is going through that lunatic head of yours—wait.”

[P97]
Won Myunghoon had been about to smack the Guild member when he stopped.

[P98]
He had only meant for them to keep Jonghun quiet with Silence magic or whatever else was necessary.

[P99]
But did they really need to?

[P100]
*Come to think of it, no one knows more about my secrets than he does.*

[P101]
He had used Jonghun as his right-hand man for a full ten years. The man had a certain low cunning, and his skills as a Hunter were excellent.

[P102]
Even when that incident had occurred eight years ago, Won Myunghoon had believed that Team Leader 1, if no one else, would never betray him.

[P103]
*Because if he opened his mouth, he wouldn’t get off unscathed either.*

[P104]
It wasn’t a matter of trust, but mutual interests.

[P105]
The scale of their greed might differ, but in a sense, the two of them were cut from the same cloth.

[P106]
But…

[P107]
*He’s useless now.*

[P108]
Won Myunghoon had seen plenty of people exposed to the Fear of high-level monsters.

[P109]
Their symptoms varied, but they all had one thing in common.

[P110]
*Junk.*

[P111]
Once fear had been branded into their souls, they could never return to the way they had been.

[P112]
Some went mad and were locked away in special wards. Even those who managed to recover could consider their lives as Hunters over.

[P113]
*He knows more about my secrets than anyone, and he’s the one who personally acquired Yeti’s Necklace.*

[P114]
On top of that, his credentials as an A-Rank Hunter were now worth no more than the paper they were printed on.

[P115]
Won Myunghoon deliberated only briefly, then reached his decision even faster.

[P116]
“Tie him up. I have a use for him.”

[P117]
“What?”

[P118]
“When that Named Monster comes, don’t you think we’ll need at least one piece of bait to throw it?”

[P119]
“……!”

[P120]
“It works out well in more ways than one. Since Jin Taekyung is dead, we ought to lose an A-Rank Hunter on our side too. It’ll make the story more convincing.”

[P121]
Won Myunghoon patted the frozen Guild member on the shoulder as he passed, then concealed himself in the nearby undergrowth.

[P122]
*Come on. Anyone.*

[P123]
He didn’t have to wait long.

[P124]
When he saw two people emerge through the undergrowth several dozen meters away, the corners of his mouth lifted.

[P125]
*The old Guild Master and Jin Taekyung. Are the others all dead?*

[P126]
Jin Taekyung was drenched in blood from head to toe, with an old mage on his back.

[P127]
No matter how Won Myunghoon looked at them, they resembled nothing so much as wounded survivors of a lost battle.

[P128]
*This should be easy.*

[P129]
Jin Taekyung in particular—Won Myunghoon wanted to kill that bastard with his own hands.

[P130]
He had just finished preparing to signal the Guild members when—

[P131]
“Come out, you fucking bastards.”

[P132]
Jin Taekyung crooked a finger directly at the undergrowth where Won Myunghoon was hiding.

[P133]
The smile vanished from Won Myunghoon’s lips.

[P134]
* * *

[P135]
“Would you look at this insolent bastard.”

[P136]
Seeing Won Myunghoon’s twisted face, I couldn’t help but laugh under my breath.

[P137]
How should I put it? I felt like I’d just seen how low a human being could sink.

[P138]
“You’re laughing?”

[P139]
Apparently, my reaction made him even angrier. He licked his dry lips and exhaled a hot breath.

[P140]
“You bastard…do you not understand what kind of situation you’re in?”

[P141]
“I understand perfectly.”

[P142]
“And you’re still standing there grinning?”

[P143]
“Choose your words carefully. Hearing you say that makes me want to split your head open.”

[P144]
“……What?”

[P145]
“You should’ve stopped when I called you Mr. Won Myunghoon. Won Myunghoon, you fucking bastard.”

[P146]
The hyenas’ faces went blank.

[P147]
Won Myunghoon’s lips remained tightly sealed for a long moment before finally opening.

[P148]
“Have you lost your mind?”

[P149]
“I’m as sane as ever. Aren’t I, Butler Kim?”

[P150]
Still on my back and watching the situation unfold, Butler Kim answered.

[P151]
“Entirely normal. Never losing one’s composure, no matter the situation, is one of the basic qualities a Hunter should possess.”

[P152]
“What about that bastard?”

[P153]
“If this had happened during the Great Cataclysm, we wouldn’t have found so much as his corpse. Those were somewhat rougher times.”

[P154]
“That’s what he says.”

[P155]
Bang!

[P156]
A single punch shattered a tree thick enough for a man to wrap both arms around.

[P157]
Won Myunghoon’s face flushed bright red as he glared at Butler Kim and me.

[P158]
“You fucking bastards!”

[P159]
“What an insolent bastard. There’s nothing he won’t say to an elder. Right?”

[P160]
Butler Kim answered calmly.

[P161]
“The young man does seem somewhat lacking in manners. But isn’t this a good world we live in? We should give him a chance.”

[P162]
“Is that so?”

[P163]
“Life is a series of choices. And from what I can see, you appear to have already made yours.”

[P164]
“You’re a ghost.”

[P165]
“I don’t particularly care for that word. I am somewhat advanced in age, after all.”

[P166]
“Sorry. I didn’t mean anything by it.”

[P167]
“I’ll get down now. One, two, three.”

[P168]
Crack.

[P169]
Butler Kim hopped off my back, and his knee gave an alarming crack.

[P170]
“Oh dear, are you all right?”

[P171]
“My knee has been troubling me. Heal.”

[P172]
When the glow faded, he tapped his knee a few times and smiled.

[P173]
“I’m fine now.”

[P174]
“Wow.”

[P175]
Magic really was incredibly convenient.

[P176]
After letting out a quiet exclamation, I turned toward the knife-sharp gazes stabbing at me from every direction.

[P177]
A dozen or so Star Guild members, Won Myunghoon included, glared at us as though they wanted to tear us apart.

[P178]
“What the fuck are you trying to do?”

[P179]
“What else? I helped him down. I thought he might get shaken around too much during the fight.”

[P180]
“Fight?”

[P181]
“What? Didn’t you come here to fight me?”

[P182]
“Of course not.”

[P183]
Won Myunghoon added with a savage laugh,

[P184]
“We came to kill every last one of you.”

[P185]
“Oh… You sound exactly like a villain in a web novel.”

[P186]
I was fairly impressed.

[P187]
At the same time, the last of my hesitation faded, and my mind became clear.

[P188]
*Right. I just had to do it.*

[P189]
“Thanks for saying that. My headache’s completely gone. Maybe you’re not a son of a bitch after all—maybe you’re Dogvorin.”[^1]

[P190]
“You bastard!”

[P191]
“Or not. Here I come.”

[P192]
“……What?”

[P193]
Whoosh!

[P194]
I suddenly found myself wondering what expression Won Myunghoon was wearing.

[P195]
But then I realized it didn’t matter.

[P196]
Whatever expression he had worn until now, the one he was about to make had already been decided.

[P197]
“Bear with the pain. No crying.”

[P198]
Crack!

[P199]
He spun around in alarm, swinging his arm, but I caught it and twisted.

[P200]
The bone snapped in an instant. His grip went limp, and the spear slipped from his hand.

[P201]
His smooth, unlined face twisted like a demon’s as a scream burst from his throat.

[P202]
“Gyaaaaaaaaaaah!”

[P203]
“Didn’t I tell you?”

[P204]
I continued in a calm voice.

[P205]
“Never bare your teeth at me again.”

[P206]
At the same time, I drove my tightly clenched fist into his maw.

[P207]
Crunch!

# Translation Rules

## Fidelity

- Translate the Korean source—not the wiki, manhwa, fan translations, or expected plot.
- Semantic fidelity outranks elegance. Never improve rhythm, humor, or localization by changing a physical action, negation, relationship, hierarchy, mechanism, quantity, or causal detail.

- Preserve small action verbs and pragmatic cues exactly: nodding versus shaking one's head, pretending nothing happened, and mild or approachable impressions are characterization, not expendable texture.
- Preserve viewpoint and tense. Resolve omitted subjects only when context supports it; retain genuine ambiguity.
- Match each speaker's hierarchy, intimacy, humor, and profanity naturally. Do not mechanically retain every honorific or classical self-reference.
- Do not censor or soften content.

## Terminology

- `compendium.md` and `docs/NAMES.md` are binding for established names, titles, ranks, techniques, organizations, system terms, items, and locations. Profile headings and aliases join that ledger.
- Search only exact Korean terms already present in the current chapter; the compendium contains future-sensitive entries.

- In System panels, render `등급` as `**Grade:**` for quest, item, skill, and martial-art classifications. Reserve `rank` for Hunter classifications or ordinary prose; never replace a System `Grade` field with `Rank`.

## English and Markdown

- Use contemporary US English and natural action-comedy prose; avoid Korean syntax calques and generic cultivation MTL phrasing.
- File: `translations/NNNN.md`; heading: `# Chapter N`.
- Speech: curly double quotes. Direct thoughts: italics without quotes.
- Use em dashes without spaces, the ellipsis character `…`, and `* * *` for source scene breaks.
- Format each actual game System-message panel as one Markdown blockquote window headed `> **System**`. Keep all consecutive notices, fields, and lines inside that same blockquote; separate windows when prose intervenes. Do not enclose System notices or UI terms in square brackets; the `System` heading and framed blockquote identify the panel. Do not label manuals, ordinary quotations, warnings printed in a manual, or other non-System material as `System`; use a normal blockquote or a specific heading instead. Do not wrap each complete notice in outer `**`; retain bold only for meaningful labels or emphasis inside the panel.
- Keep the final file English-only reading copy: no audit notes, Korean text, summaries, or model metadata.

### Tone and Style

- Write like a polished commercial webnovel: brisk, vivid, accessible, and easy to read aloud.
- Preserve the series’ contrast between danger and comedy. Let absurdity, bad timing, blunt reactions, and grim situations create dark humor without adding jokes absent from the Korean.
- Jin Taekyung’s narration is conversational, observant, self-mocking, and occasionally profane. It may be irreverent even when the situation is serious.
- Keep deadpan punchlines short and well-timed. Do not explain a joke after delivering it.
- Preserve the source's level of explicitness. A euphemism may remain euphemistic even when its meaning is sexual or crude; do not replace it with more graphic English merely for impact.
- Make dialogue spontaneous and character-specific. Preserve hierarchy and intimacy through word choice, address, rhythm, and restraint—not archaic wuxia English.
- Use strong profanity when the Korean is strong, but neither intensify nor sanitize it. Do not make ordinary lines uniformly vulgar. Profanity should reveal mood or relationship.

Keep all consecutive notices, fields, and lines inside that same blockquote; separate windows when prose intervenes. Do not enclose System notices or UI terms in square brackets; the `System` heading and framed blockquote identify the panel. Do not label manuals, ordinary quotations, warnings printed in a manual, or other non-System material as `System`; use a normal blockquote or a specific heading instead. Do not wrap each complete notice in outer `**`; retain bold only for meaningful labels or emphasis inside the panel.
- Keep the final file English-only reading copy: no audit notes, Korean text, summaries, or model metadata.

### Tone and Style

- Write like a polished commercial webnovel: brisk, vivid, accessible, and easy to read aloud.
- Preserve the series’ contrast between danger and comedy. Let absurdity, bad timing, blunt reactions, and grim situations create dark humor without adding jokes absent from the Korean.
- Jin Taekyung’s narration is conversational, observant, self-mocking, and occasionally profane. It may be irreverent even when the situation is serious.
- Keep deadpan punchlines short and well-timed. Do not explain a joke after delivering it.
- Preserve the source's level of explicitness. A euphemism may remain euphemistic even when its meaning is sexual or crude; do not replace it with more graphic English merely for impact.
- Make dialogue spontaneous and character-specific. Preserve hierarchy and intimacy through word choice, address, rhythm, and restraint—not archaic wuxia English.
- Use strong profanity when the Korean is strong, but neither intensify nor sanitize it. Do not make ordinary lines uniformly vulgar. Profanity should reveal mood or relationship.
- Keep action and injury vivid but clear rather than purple. Do not make violence funny unless the source’s framing does.
- Avoid stiff literalism, translator-added melodrama, dated internet slang, and quippy superhero-style banter.
- On the second pass, correct awkward English collocations and word choices without changing meaning or voice. Prefer ordinary, spoken English over stiff Latinate or ceremonial wording when the scene is brisk or comic: “goose bumps” rather than “gooseflesh,” and “laid into them” rather than “launched into a solemn denunciation.” Read the prose aloud and replace any phrase that sounds like a formal essay, legal document, or literal dictionary gloss unless the source deliberately calls for that register.

## Footnotes

Use `[^1]` Markdown footnotes when a brief, factual, spoiler-free explanation materially helps an English reader understand:

- a Korean institution, living arrangement, food, holiday, myth, historical reference, or local custom;
- a Korean word, phrase, idiom, wordplay, or culturally specific image that cannot be conveyed fully by the best natural English analogy;
- a deliberately literal rendering whose cultural or linguistic force would otherwise be lost.

For example, render `고시원` as “goshiwon” when the setting or connotations matter, with a concise footnote explaining that it is a very small, inexpensive room-for-rent housing arrangement. Prefer the best natural English analogy in the prose. Use a literal translation plus a concise footnote when the Korean wording itself matters. Define a term at its first meaningful occurrence and do not repeat the note unnecessarily. Footnotes must be rare, useful, and non-spoiling; do not footnote ordinary vocabulary, fully preserved jokes, or uncertainty. Record consequential uncertainty in `docs/STATE.md`.

# Adjudication Task — Chapter 224

## Korean source

```text
  1|＃224화
  2|
  3|
  4|
  5|몇 시간 전, 전력을 다해 게이트 입구로 돌아가던 십여 명의 스타 길드원들을 멈춰 세운 것은 원명훈의 외침이었다.
  6|
  7|“잠깐, 모두 정지!”
  8|
  9|모두의 시선이 그를 향해 쏠렸다.
 10|
 11|당장 뒤에서 무시무시한 네임드 몬스터가 등장할지도 모른다는 긴장감 속, 홀로 골똘히 생각에 잠겨 있던 원명훈의 입술이 열렸다.
 12|
 13|“정찰.”
 14|
 15|“예. 길드장님.”
 16|
 17|정찰 임무를 맡은 길드원이 즉각 대답했다.
 18|
 19|발이 빠르고 활을 잘 다루는 그는 제비뽑기라는 행운 덕분에 다른 동료들과 달리 간신히 죽음을 피했다.
 20|
 21|“현 위치 읊어 봐.”
 22|
 23|“좌표상 175. 37. 990입니다.”
 24|
 25|“좌표는 지랄, 게이트 입구까지 얼마 남았냐고.”
 26|
 27|“지금까지 속도를 봤을 때 약 7분 정도가 소요될 것 같습니다.”
 28|
 29|“얼마 안 남았네? 게이트 입구로 가는 길은 이곳뿐이지?”
 30|
 31|“……예. 그렇긴 합니다만.”
 32|
 33|정찰대원이 찝찝한 얼굴로 말꼬리를 흐렸다.
 34|
 35|뭔가 이상한 흐름을 느낀 다른 길드원들도 눈빛을 주고받던 그때, 불안감을 현실로 만드는 한 마디가 들려왔다.
 36|
 37|“여기서 포위망 펼친다.”
 38|
 39|“예?”
 40|
 41|“포위망이라니. 이 상황에서 말입니까?”
 42|
 43|“길드장님, 그건!”
 44|
 45|평소였다면 군말 없이 따랐을 길드원들의 반발에 원명훈의 눈빛이 차갑게 식었다.
 46|
 47|“다들 닥치고 명령 따라. 내가 다 생각이 있어서 그런 거니까.”
 48|
 49|“그래도 이건 아닙니다! 상대는 네임드 몬스터, 컥!”
 50|
 51|가장 크게 목소리를 높이던 길드원의 목을 잡아챈 원명훈이 으르렁거렸다.
 52|
 53|“게이트에서, 그것도 길드장 명령에 항명해? 이 새끼가 죽고 싶어서 환장했나…….”
 54|
 55|그야말로 순식간에 벌어진 일.
 56|
 57|장내의 분위기가 싸늘하게 얼어붙었다. 이 자리의 모두는 원명훈의 말이 비단 한 사람을 겨냥한 것이 아니라는 사실을 알고 있었다.
 58|
 59|지난 수년 동안 지켜본 바로는 능히 행동으로 옮길만한 위인이라는 것도.
 60|
 61|“죄, 죄송합니다.”
 62|
 63|“마지막 기회다. 두 번은 없어.”
 64|
 65|털썩.
 66|
 67|하얗게 질린 얼굴로 주저앉은 길드원을 뒤로하고 돌아선 원명훈이 날카로운 시선으로 주위를 훑었다.
 68|
 69|“병신 같은 놈들.”
 70|
 71|필터링을 거치지 않은 폭언에도 십여 쌍의 고개는 땅만 응시했다.
 72|
 73|이미 지난 수년 동안 원명훈이라는 인간을 충분히 겪어 본 그들에게는 익숙한 일이다.
 74|
 75|게이트에서는 더더욱 조심해야 했다. 그는 A급 헌터, 이 자리의 모두가 달려들어도 이길 수 없는 강자다.
 76|
 77|“대가리가 그렇게 안 굴러가나? 내가 네임드 몬스터를 상대할 만큼 멍청한 놈으로 보여?”
 78|
 79|푹 수그리고 있던 고개들이 슬그머니 올라왔다.
 80|
 81|“그럼…….”
 82|
 83|“그 떨거지들을 처리한다.”
 84|
 85|“떨거지들이라면, 평화 길드 말입니까?”
 86|
 87|“지금쯤이면 전멸하고도 남았을 것 같은데요.”
 88|
 89|그들은 정신없이 도망치는 와중에 괴수의 포효를 들었다. 듣는 것만으로도 오금이 저리고 등골이 오싹해지는, 그건 말 그대로 공포 그 자체였다.
 90|
 91|비록 어떻게 생긴 놈인지 확인은 못 했지만 그렇기에 지금까지 살아 있을 수 있었다.
 92|
 93|‘그런 놈을 겨우 다섯이서 어떻게 상대해. 이미 다 죽었지.’
 94|
 95|이것이 모두의 공통된 의견이었다.
 96|
 97|그러나 오직 한 사람, 원명훈만큼은 달랐다.
 98|
 99|“만약 한 놈이라도 살아남아 도망친다면?”
100|
101|“그, 그건…….”
102|
103|“설마요.”
104|
105|거기까지는 미처 생각해 보지 못한 문제다.
106|
107|평소였다면 달랐을 텐데, 네임드 몬스터에 대한 두려움과 생존 욕구가 불러온 사고의 마비였다.
108|
109|우물쭈물하는 길드원들을 향해 원명훈이 확고한 어조로 말했다.
110|
111|“만에 하나 그 떨거지 중에 단 한 놈이라도 살아서 게이트를 빠져나가면, 우리 전부 인생 종 치는 거다.”
112|
113|“…….”
114|
115|“언론의 스포트라이트를 듬뿍 받고 있던 A급 헌터가 죽었다. 그리고 유일하게 살아남은 평화 길드원 중 하나가 우리 이야기를 꺼낸다? 그 후는 굳이 말 안 해도 대충 알겠지.”
116|
117|언론, 아니 전 국민의 관심이 그들을 향해 쏠린다.
118|
119|수사기관이 움직이고, 언론과 대중 미디어는 이 문제를 매우 비중 있게 다루며 연일 새로운 보도를 쏟아 낼 것이다.
120|
121|설령 생존자가 명확한 증언과 물증을 제시하지 못한다고 해도, 그들이 받을 멸시와 비난은 사라지지 않는다.
122|
123|어쩌면 이 나라를 떠나야 할지도 모른다. 부모님 성묘를 위해 비자를 발급받아야 하는 처지. 상상만 해도 끔찍했다.
124|
125|“가끔은 사실보다는 사람들의 인식이 중요하지. 너희도 8년 전에 이미 겪어 봤잖아?”
126|
127|“길드장님!”
128|
129|“그건!”
130|
131|격렬한 동요가 스타 길드원들 사이로 퍼져 나갔다.
132|
133|그것은 암묵적인 금기어였다. 그런데 다름 아닌 원명훈이 직접 이런 이야기를 꺼낼 줄이야.
134|
135|심지어 그는 모든 일을 계획하고 자신들을 포섭했던 사람 아닌가?
136|
137|길드원들의 사나워진 눈빛에 원명훈이 피식 웃었다.
138|
139|“눈 깔아. 이 개새끼들아. 죄다 뽑아 버리기 전에.”
140|
141|“……!”
142|
143|“너희가 원해서 가담한 거잖아. 여기에 내 돈 안 받아먹은 새끼 있어? 그 돈으로 집 사고, 차 사고, 술이며 여자며 실컷 즐기다가 결혼해서 애 낳고. 좋은 아빠인 척, 성실한 남편인 척하면서 잘 살고 있잖아?”
144|
145|원명훈이 신경질적으로 머리카락을 쓸었다. 그의 번뜩이는 눈빛이 스쳐 지나갈 때마다 사람들의 몸이 떨렸다.
146|
147|부정하고 싶지만, 그의 입에서 나온 말은 모두 사실이었다.
148|
149|그들은 이미 돌아올 수 없는 강을 건넜고, 그들을 배에 실어 강 너머로 옮긴 건 원명훈이었다.
150|
151|뱃사공은 이미 배를 숨겼다. 그의 허락이 없다면 다시 강 저편으로 돌아갈 수 없다.
152|
153|숨이 끊기기 전까지는.
154|
155|“더 이상 길게 말 안 한다. 숨어서 포위망 펼쳐. 내 신호가 떨어지면 누구든 죽여 버릴 수 있게.”
156|
157|원명훈의 살기 어린 목소리는 대법원의 판결문이나 다름없었다.
158|
159|항소 따위는 통하지 않는다는 것을 깨달은 사람들이 뿔뿔이 흩어져 포위망을 형성하기 시작했다.
160|
161|“병신 같은 새끼들. 벌써 8년이나 지난 일을.”
162|
163|씹어뱉듯이 중얼거리던 원명훈에게 한 길드원이 쭈뼛거리며 다가왔다.
164|
165|“저, 길드장님.”
166|
167|“왜.”
168|
169|“1팀장님, 아니 1팀장은 어떻게 할까요?”
170|
171|“김종훈이? 그 새끼 지금 어디 있어?”
172|
173|“우선은 저기에 옮겨 놨습니다.”
174|

Keep SOL when it is slangier, punchier, more spoken, or more idiomatic and the Korean sense holds (`기만질` → “con me”, `톡톡히` → “full Peak Master treatment”, `득실거리다` → “crawling with”, `인간 백정` → “butcher of men”, `한 몸` → “are one”, `시원하다` in a bath → “That’s the stuff”, `어렵게 찾아오고 쉽게 깨지는 법` → “hard-won and easily broken”). If SOL already naturalized Korean syntax (`이 혁무진` → “I, Hyuk Mujin”), keep SOL. Do not reproduce Korean word order.

**Literal closeness to Korean wording is not fidelity.** Preserve the source’s meaning and effect in natural English.

## Veto — choose `BASE`

Use `BASE` only for a real miss:

* wrong denotation, quantity, hedge, category, subject/object, or physical action
* a different English idiom than the Korean joke (`까발리다` ≠ “gives someone away”; `넉살` ≠ “banter”)
* a rebuilt joke whose comic machine BASE already has (`얼마나 …는지 …겠다` must stay a simple exaggeration: “snored so loudly even my mother in Ilsan probably heard him,” not “You had to wonder how loudly…”)
* dropped image, attitude, or timing
* SOL replaces an established project rendering, System label, or Markdown convention with an unsupported synonym
* SOL stamps `hyung` (or another kinship title) onto every narrative name when BASE already uses the name and the Korean `형` is ordinary reference, not a vocative or a topical joke (`진호 형` → Jinho in narration)

Do not veto SOL for being informal. Do not veto SOL to “clarify” slang. Do not veto SOL merely because BASELINE is already understandable.

## `REPAIR` only when both fail

Example: `겹경사가 따로 없다` means two good things **together** (double blessing). `따로` is not “separate.” If BASE says “entirely separate stroke of luck” and SOL says “unexpected windfall,” `REPAIR` to stacked luck.

Do not `REPAIR` a working SOL line. Do not invent a third style because you prefer it.

For `REPAIR`, write the smallest complete replacement needed for that hunk. It must be natural English and fully source-faithful.

## Glossary

Korean **keys** are binding unless the source uses that string in a different ordinary-language sense. Glossary **English** is not a license for a calque (`presiding chair`). If SOL is a natural recast of the same sense, keep SOL.

Return exactly one JSON object and no Markdown fence or prose:

Include exactly one decision for every numbered hunk, in hunk order. `replacement` is required only for `REPAIR`.

Reasons must name the veto, or say that SOL keeps sense and voice. Do not merely say one version is "better" or "more natural" without stating what changed.

Keep reasons brief. Do not adjudicate unchanged passages. Do not call tools.

## Critical binding translation rules

# Translation Rules

## Fidelity

- Translate the Korean source—not the wiki, manhwa, fan translations, or expected plot.
- Semantic fidelity outranks elegance. Never improve rhythm, humor, or localization by changing a physical action, negation, relationship, hierarchy, mechanism, quantity, or causal detail.
- Preserve every fact, causal link, joke, emotional beat, repetition, and intentional omission. Add nothing.
- Preserve small action verbs and pragmatic cues exactly: nodding versus shaking one's head, pretending nothing happened, and mild or approachable impressions are characterization, not expendable texture.
- Preserve viewpoint and tense. Resolve omitted subjects only when context supports it; retain genuine ambiguity.
- Match each speaker's hierarchy, intimacy, humor, and profanity naturally. Do not mechanically retain every honorific or classical self-reference.
- Do not censor or soften content.

## Terminology

- `compendium.md` and `docs/NAMES.md` are binding for established names, titles, ranks, techniques, organizations, system terms, items, and locations. Profile headings and aliases join that ledger.
- Search only exact Korean terms already present in the current chapter; the compendium contains future-sensitive entries.
- Never re-romanize established names or invent grand names for uncertain terms. First use of an unlisted name or title almost always needs a footnote or a mapped ledger term.
- Use `qi` for Murim energy and `mana` for the modern Hunter system when the source distinguishes them. Preserve an established chapter-specific rendering such as `internal energy` when the exact glossary and surrounding Korean distinguish accumulated `공력` from resulting `기운`.
- In System panels, render `등급` as `**Grade:**` for quest, item, skill, and martial-art classifications. Reserve `rank` for Hunter classifications or ordinary prose; never replace a System `Grade` field with `Rank`.

## English and Markdown

- Use contemporary US English and natural action-comedy prose; avoid Korean syntax calques and generic cultivation MTL phrasing.
- File: `translations/NNNN.md`; heading: `# Chapter N`.
- Speech: curly double quotes. Direct thoughts: italics without quotes.
- Use em dashes without spaces, the ellipsis character `…`, and `* * *` for source scene breaks.
- Format each actual game System-message panel as one Markdown blockquote window headed `> **System**`. Keep all consecutive notices, fields, and lines inside that same blockquote; separate windows when prose intervenes. Do not enclose System notices or UI terms in square brackets; the `System` heading and framed blockquote identify the panel. Do not label manuals, ordinary quotations, warnings printed in a manual, or other non-System material as `System`; use a normal blockquote or a specific heading instead. Do not wrap each complete notice in outer `**`; retain bold only for meaningful labels or emphasis inside the panel.
- Keep the final file English-only reading copy: no audit notes, Korean text, summaries, or model metadata.

### Tone and Style

- Write like a polished commercial webnovel: brisk, vivid, accessible, and easy to read aloud.
- Preserve the series’ contrast between danger and comedy. Let absurdity, bad timing, blunt reactions, and grim situations create dark humor without adding jokes absent from the Korean.
- Jin Taekyung’s narration is conversational, observant, self-mocking, and occasionally profane. It may be irreverent even when the situation is serious.
- Keep deadpan punchlines short and well-timed. Do not explain a joke after delivering it.
- Preserve the source's level of explicitness. A euphemism may remain euphemistic even when its meaning is sexual or crude; do not replace it with more graphic English merely for impact.
- Make dialogue spontaneous and character-specific. Preserve hierarchy and intimacy through word choice, address, rhythm, and restraint—not archaic wuxia English.
- Use strong profanity when the Korean is strong, but neither intensify nor sanitize it. Do not make ordinary lines uniformly vulgar. Profanity should reveal mood or relationship.
- Keep action and injury vivid but clear rather than purple. Do not make violence funny unless the source’s framing does.
- Avoid stiff literalism, translator-added melodrama, dated internet slang, and quippy superhero-style banter.
- On the second pass, correct awkward English collocations and word choices without changing meaning or voice. Prefer ordinary, spoken English over stiff Latinate or ceremonial wording when the scene is brisk or comic: “goose bumps” rather than “gooseflesh,” and “laid into them” rather than “launched into a solemn denunciation.” Read the prose aloud and replace any phrase that sounds like a formal essay, legal document, or literal dictionary gloss unless the source deliberately calls for that register.

## Footnotes

Use `[^1]` Markdown footnotes when a brief, factual, spoiler-free explanation materially helps an English reader understand:

- a Korean institution, living arrangement, food, holiday, myth, historical reference, or local custom;
- a Korean word, phrase, idiom, wordplay, or culturally specific image that cannot be conveyed fully by the best natural English analogy;
- a deliberately literal rendering whose cultural or linguistic force would otherwise be lost.

For example, render `고시원` as “goshiwon” when the setting or connotations matter, with a concise footnote explaining that it is a very small, inexpensive room-for-rent housing arrangement. Prefer the best natural English analogy in the prose. Use a literal translation plus a concise footnote when the Korean wording itself matters. Define a term at its first meaningful occurrence and do not repeat the note unnecessarily. Footnotes must be rare, useful, and non-spoiling; do not footnote ordinary vocabulary, fully preserved jokes, or uncertainty. Record consequential uncertainty in `docs/STATE.md`.

## Spoilers and Scope

- Safe profiles contain only facts revealed through the latest completed chapter.
- Never read `characters/spoilers/` during drafting. Reviewers may consult one relevant sealed profile only for a specific unresolved continuity issue after the draft is complete.
- Future knowledge may prevent contradiction but may not add early names, pronouns, certainty, motives, or foreshadowing.
- Translate exactly one requested chapter unless the user explicitly requests a batch. Never modify Korean source files under `source/`.
